'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[Duwa Lashi La]], leader of the anti-junta [[National Unity Government of Myanmar|National Unity Government]], calls for a national revolt and uprising against the military government led by [[Min Aung Hlaing]] and for a "defensive war" in "every corner of the country; every village, town and city". [https://www.dw.com/en/myanmar-resistance-group-calls-for-revolt-against-military/a-59106630 (Deutsche Welle)]
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Guinean coup d'état]]
**As the military consolidates power in the country, Colonel [[Mamady Doumbouya]] vows to free all "political prisoners" without mentioning any specific people or referring to deposed president [[Alpha Condé]]. Condé opposition groups welcome the news but say that no prisoners have been released. [https://www.dw.com/en/guinea-coup-leaders-promise-to-free-political-prisoners/a-59112681 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[2021 Afghan protests]]
**Around 300 to 500 protesters, including women, took to the streets of [[Kabul]]. The [[Taliban]] used gunfire, detentions and beatings to disperse the crowds. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/09/07/asia/afghanistan-tuesday-kabul-protests-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**Gunmen [[kidnap]] 18 villagers in [[Kaduna State]], [[Nigeria]], including seven children, according to a community leader. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kidnap-18-villagers-latest-attack-northern-nigeria-2021-09-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Businesses and economy'''
*[[El Salvador]] becomes the first country in the world to adopt the [[cryptocurrency]] [[Bitcoin]] as [[legal tender]] as well as the national currency as the [[Bitcoin Law]] comes into effect. However, a small but growing number of people opposed to the new law protested against it in the capital, [[San Salvador]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/9/7/glitches-protests-as-bitcoin-becomes-legal-tender-in-el-salvador (Al Jazeera English)] [https://www.wsj.com/articles/bitcoin-comes-to-el-salvador-first-country-to-adopt-crypto-as-national-currency-11631005200 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Guerrero earthquake]]
**A 7.0 magnitude [[list of earthquakes in Mexico|earthquake]] struck just outside the [[tourism in Mexico|tourist]] city of [[Acapulco]], [[Guerrero]], [[Mexico]], killing at least one person and leaving more than 1.6 million without electricity. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/magnitude-74-quake-strikes-mexico-usgs-2021-09-08/ (Reuters)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/08/mexico-earthquake-tsunami-warning-acapulco (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****The [[Indonesia]]n [[National Agency of Drug and Food Control of Indonesia|Drug and Food Control Authority]] issues emergency use authorizations for the single-dose [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine|Janssen]] vaccine and the [[CanSino Biologics|CanSino]] [[Convidecia]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5713795/bpom-setujui-vaksin-covid-19-janssen-sekali-suntik-dan-vaksin-cansino (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Japan]]
****The [[Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare]] signs a agreement with the [[Takeda Pharmaceutical Company]] to purchase 150 million doses of the [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]] that will be manufactured and distributed domestically by Takeda beginning next year. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/09/07/national/japan-secures-150-million-novavax/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 3,963 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 240,042. [https://www.montsame.mn/en/read/274362 (Montsame)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports 328 new locally transmitted cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total in more than a year. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/328-new-locally-transmitted-covid-19-cases-in-singapore-including-185-unlinked (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Spain]]
****The [[Spain|Spanish]] Public Health Commission approves the administration of a third "[[booster dose|booster]]" dose of the COVID-19 vaccine for severely [[Immunosuppression|immunosuppresse]]d people. [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2021/09/07/spains-public-health-commission-approves-third-covid-vaccine-dose-for-immunosuppressed-people/ (''Euro Weekly News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports its first two cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Mu variant]], which was originally detected in [[Colombia]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/turkey-confirms-first-cases-of-coronavirus-mu-variant/2357936 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***The number of [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] due to COVID-19 in [[Africa]] surpasses 200,000. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa-covid-death-toll-tops-200-000-afp-tally (Radio France Internationale)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Caledonia]]
***The [[French overseas department]] of [[New Caledonia]] enters a two-week [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after three community transmitted COVID-19 cases were reported yesterday. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/450910/new-caledonia-goes-into-lockdown-after-covid-19-community-outbreak (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***[[Venezuela]] receives their first shipment of 693,600 doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[Coronavac]] vaccine supplied through the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-07/south-america-s-least-vaccinated-country-gets-first-covax-shots?utm_source=google&utm_medium=bd&cmpId=google (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 40 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.usnews.com/news/health-news/articles/2021-09-08/us-covid-19-cases-now-top-40-million (''U.S. News & World Report'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Abortion in Mexico]]
**In a unanimous vote, the Mexican [[Supreme Court of Mexico|Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation]] rules that criminalizing [[abortion]] is unconstitutional, setting a precedent for the legalization of abortion. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/07/world/americas/mexico-supreme-court-decriminalize-abortion.html (The New York Times)]
*[[Human Rights Watch]] accuses security forces in [[Egypt]] of killing 755 people, mainly members of the [[Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt|Muslim Brotherhood]], during [[Extrajudicial killing|extrajudicial execution]]s, between 2015 and 2020. Security forces claimed that the deaths only occurred during "shootouts". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58475287 (BBC News)]
*The [[Supreme Court of Cape Verde]] approves the extradition of [[Alex Saab]] to the [[United States]] for alleged money laundering on behalf of the [[Government of Venezuela|Venezuelan government]]. Saab was arrested in [[Cape Verde]] in June 2020, when his plane stopped there for refuelling while flying to [[Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/cape-verde-court-approves-extradition-maduro-envoy-us-2021-09-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**On [[Independence Day (Brazil)|Independence Day]], [[President of Brazil|Brazilian president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] and his main opponent, former president [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]], hold rallies in different cities to mark the anniversary. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/09/07/bolsonaro-and-lula-da-silva-plan-rallies-on-tuesday-brazil-s-independence-day (MercoPress)]
**During the rallies, Bolsonaro alleges that next year's [[2022 Brazilian general election|presidential election]] would be a "farce" and criticizes the [[Supreme Federal Court]] for investigating him and his allies. [https://www.reuters.com/news/picture/bolsonaro-supporters-march-against-brazi-idUSRTXGU2AF (Reuters)] [https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/politica/bolsonaro-discurso-manifestacao-avenida-paulista/ (CNN Brazil)] 
**[[Gettr]] [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] and former [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign|Donald Trump 2020 campaign]] adviser [[Jason Miller (communications strategist)|Jason Miller]] is detained following a [[Conservative Political Action Conference#Brazil|CPAC]] event in Brazil. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/trump-jason-miller-brazil-bolsonaro/2021/09/07/a3422d10-0ff8-11ec-bc8a-8d9a5b534194_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/jason-miller-trump-questioned-brazil-b1915819.html (''The Independent'')] 
*[[Politics of Afghanistan]]
**The Taliban names [[Mohammad Hassan Akhund]] as the leader of [[Afghanistan]] and [[Abdul Ghani Baradar]] as the deputy leader of the country. Akhund was an associate of the late [[Mullah Omar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/taliban-fire-air-scatter-kabul-protesters-no-reports-injuries-2021-09-07/ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/7/profile-mullah-baradar-afghanistans-new-leader (Al Jazeera)]
